A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same GAPL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, controlled comparisons, ablations, robustness experiments, and attention analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including GAPL benchmark scores and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage method remains unchanged: frozen-encoder MLP training and PCA prototype extraction, followed by LoRA adaptation and cross-attention prototype mapping. The architecture, objectives, and inference procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same prototype sources, Community Forensics training data, six evaluation benchmarks with 55 subsets, generator-scaling datasets, and post-processing scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 3, and 6–11 and the robustness comparison in Figure 6. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported training data sizes, 5% validation split, accuracy threshold of 0.5, preprocessing, training schedules, and comparison procedures remain unchanged. The introduction's metric-label correction does not change the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, prototype-number and generator-selection analyses, JPEG/blur robustness tests, prototype examples, and Appendix F attention visualizations are retained. Relocating Figure 5 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 6–9 and 11 newly append dispersion-like ± terms to existing mean accuracy and AP values. Neither their statistical definition nor repeated-run or seed information is supplied, so this establishes a reporting addition rather than additional runs or a new experimental design.

E6.justification: New numerical dispersion entries supplement existing results; for example, GAPL's ForenSynths means become 97.2 ± 3.6 accuracy and 99.5 ± 1.1 AP in Table 6. Existing point estimates, rankings, and plotted findings remain unchanged; no performance improvement between versions is demonstrated.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16, the Gaussian-mixture variance argument, LDA formulation, prototype construction, and Appendix F.1 variance-bound derivation are retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects its quantitative summary: v1 incorrectly calls 94.9% average accuracy, while v2 identifies 90.4% accuracy and 94.9% average precision, matching Table 1 in both versions. The central scalability, methodological, and performance claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The data-heterogeneity and frozen-encoder explanations, interpretations of ablations and robustness, and limitations concerning genuinely unseen future generators are substantively retained. The conclusion, limitations, and robustness discussion are rephrased without introducing a new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix E retain the same backbone, MLP dimensions, LoRA settings, optimizer, preprocessing, stopping criteria, and two RTX 4090 GPUs. The code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations on image-adaptive prompt learning, Beyond Artifacts, and MIRROR while retaining the existing research positioning. The duplicate GenImage references are consolidated, rather than a distinct cited work being removed.

P1.justification: The introduction's method summary, robustness discussion, conclusion, and limitations receive localized rewrites. The title changes 'via' to 'with,' acknowledgments are expanded, and minor wording is corrected; the overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7, Table 2 changes position within page 6, and surrounding text reflows. Appendix tables resize to accommodate expanded mean entries. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through the corrected accuracy/AP summary, tighter prose, and updated related-work coverage. The added dispersion values remain undefined, and two entries omit the ± separator, limiting their statistical usefulness. The gains are editorial and reporting improvements; the method and underlying experimental evidence are unchanged.
